candidates.claim: fw-01 has telnet management access enabled (mgmt_access service telnet, src 10.10.10.0/24, interface ot), and the registry forbids telnet on any device.
candidates.remediation: Remove the telnet mgmt_access line from fw-01 and manage the firewall with SSH or HTTPS/ASDM from MGMT on the mgmt interface only.

candidates.claim: fw-01 allows device management from the OT subnet 10.10.10.0/24 on the ot interface, but the policy permits device management only from MGMT 10.10.99.0/24 and, on fw-01, only on the mgmt interface.
candidates.remediation: Remove the management access entry sourced from 10.10.10.0/24 on the ot interface and restrict management to 10.10.99.0/24 on the mgmt interface.

candidates.claim: The baseline delta shows the telnet management line 'telnet 10.10.10.0' at fw-01:116 was added relative to the approved baseline and is not part of it.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile this deviation by removing the telnet line or recording it as an approved baseline change.

clarifications.question: The zone registry assigns no zone to rtr-01 GigabitEthernet0 (10.10.99.12/24, no inbound ACL, anchor rtr-01:46) or to GigabitEthernet0/0/1 (203.0.113.1/29, no ACL, anchor rtr-01:41), and rtr-01 has two default routes (rtr-01:54 via 198.51.100.1 and rtr-01:55 via 10.10.99.1). Can OT-side or MGMT hosts reach OUTSIDE, or the firewall's outside side, through rtr-01 without passing the fw-01 MGMT_IN or OUTSIDE_IN ACLs? Please confirm the zones of these interfaces and whether rtr-01 forwards traffic between them.

fw-01 has the ASA HTTP server enabled (fw-01:109) and plaintext http management from MGMT on the mgmt interface (fw-01:110). The policy forbids IOS HTTP/HTTPS servers and requires HTTPS/ASDM, but it does not say whether plaintext ASA http management is forbidden. Should this be reported as a policy violation?
